label: early original-phase steps, boosted by inputs n/1/0/f/z/j or sequences starting with 3/l/g
explanation: Low end of candidate unit 6. 93% of activation mass falls in the original (input) phase, peaking at t=3-4. It is silent at t=0, weak at t=1, and rare after t=7 and during the copy phase; the delimiter step carries about 4% of the mass. Within that window two factors raise the firing rate and add together: (1) the current input token is n, 1, 0, f, z or j (rate 10-18% vs 5% base), and (2) the sequence started with 3, l or g (first_tok=3 has rate 23%). The top activations (~0.5) are sequences starting with 3/l/3 3 g where n, 1 or z arrives at t=3-4. It fires mostly on first occurrences of a token (89% of mass). Tokens such as t, h and o, and digit 2 / letters b, c, d, e, v as outputs, suppress it. A single boolean predicate built on position, input token and first token reaches only about 0.5 F1 (mass recall ~0.8, precision ~0.4). This suggests a graded, roughly additive dependence on token identity and prefix content rather than a crisp condition.
